title: H5 – Performance management
source: Zusammenfassung von Session 4 und 5 „Performance management“ (Cappelli & Tavis, 2016; Beach-House-Fall)

blocks.text: Before measuring, define performance: dimensions, standards, situational constraints, number of levels and absolute vs relative comparison (Latham et al., 2007).
Evaluation systems shape behaviour: team grades encourage cooperation (and free riding), rankings encourage competition (and stop sharing).
Firms drop traditional annual appraisals because of the return of people development, the need for agility and the centrality of teamwork (Cappelli & Tavis, 2016).
Forced distribution demotivates the middle, causes infighting and horse-trading, costs time, ignores diversity and fosters short-termism.
Design a PM system from its purpose (accountability, development, communication) and from the nature of the work – innovators cannot be managed like routine workers.
PM has limits: not everything valuable can be measured, and every metric has externalities.
Performance theory (Latham, Sulsky & Macdonald, 2007)

Beach House design choices
children: A Team vs Tweakers: same system?

blocks.text: 1. Diagnose: what is the business problem the PM system must solve (e.g. innovation, quality, cooperation)?
2. Define performance for each group with (a)–(e).
3. Choose the purpose and design accordingly (frequency, raters, indicators, link to pay).
4. Predict behaviour and externalities – what will people stop doing?
5. Link to rewards carefully: PRP depends entirely on the PM system.
The continuous process of defining, measuring, discussing and developing employee performance in line with organisational goals.
The formal (often annual) evaluation of an employee's performance.
Ranking employees on a fixed curve (e.g. top 20 %, middle 70 %, bottom 10 %).
Lobbying and trading favours before performance reviews.
What is pushing organizations to drop traditional performance appraisals – and what do they still need ratings for?
